about.body: The S62 is BMW M's naturally aspirated 5.0-litre V8 engine, produced from 1999 to 2003. It was fitted exclusively to the E39 M5 — the only BMW model to receive this engine. The S62 represented a significant step forward for BMW M, featuring individual throttle bodies, double-VANOS variable valve timing, and a high-revving character that set it apart from the standard M62 V8 it was derived from.

byModel.body: The S62 appears in a single application: the E39 M5 (1999–2003). This was the first M5 to use a V8 engine, replacing the S38 inline-six used in the previous generation. The E39 M5 remains one of the most highly regarded M cars ever built, and the S62 is central to its reputation — a naturally aspirated V8 with a 7,000 rpm redline and a character that modern turbocharged M engines don't replicate.

compatibility.body: Because the S62 was fitted to a single model generation (E39 M5), compatibility is more straightforward than for engines that span multiple model lines. However, the S62 shares its basic architecture with the M62 family, and some components — particularly ancillaries, engine mounts, and ECU software — are specific to the E39 M5 application.
